speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities, along with a recent history of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any other symptoms like joint pain, muscle aches, or swollen lymph nodes?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease).

The clinical picture of a pruritic rash appearing 2-3 days after the onset of "slapped cheek" or facial erythema, following a viral prodrome in a child, is classic for Parvovirus B19 infection. No further testing is required for this diagnosis.
